answer: A harbor that docks any ship for free invites a thousand fake captains. An agent economy resists sybil attacks by charging every new identity a work bond: to trade, an agent must lock stake and finish verified work first. One fake identity is cheap, but ten thousand cost ten thousand bonds plus ten thousand units of real work, and the bond is slashed when cheating is proven. Like a vine that only grows where rooted, reputation attaches to identities with history, an atlas of proven behavior, so a fresh fake cannot borrow an agent's trust. Attackers pay linearly; defenders verify once.
